correctness.rationale: Condition on the initial case: k cases detect at zero; H then has r geometric single waits, and L has one parallel minimum and r-1 sums of single and parallel waits. For the two serial stages the survival is ((1-gamma)q^t-(1-q)gamma^t)/(q-gamma), gamma=q^k; inserting it in the mixture and factoring gives the claimed difference and zero at t=0. Its positive-time prefactor is strictly positive, and summation gives the stated mean gap. S_k increases strictly from 1 to k; 1<r<k first occurs at n=5,k=3. Both rational mean witnesses agree. Replacing the two stages by independent exponentials of rates beta and k beta gives the recorded continuous factorization and mean by integration. At r=k the continuous laws tie (the discrete hub placement is then strictly better). Stochastic order optimizes nondecreasing costs when the expectations are meaningful, not necessarily strictly for flat costs. A new bounded exact convolution check verified discrete cases n=3..7, all allowed budgets, three rational p values, times 0..8, and both mean witnesses; the source checker tests discrete state transitions, not the continuous theorem.

value.rationale: The result exactly identifies when the intuitive hub-monitoring ranking fails simultaneously for every positive deadline. It distinguishes that phenomenon from an average-only ranking and shows it can disappear in the continuous-time model. This is a meaningful small-network benchmark for defensive monitoring objectives, not a general epidemiological recommendation.
